title: Grow-Space Zoning, Movement and Sanitation Flow

content.overview: A grow space is a workflow as well as a room. People, plants, tools, waste and supplies move through it, and poorly planned movement can spread contamination or create safety conflicts even when the environmental equipment is adequate.

vocabulary.definition: Dividing a workspace by function, cleanliness, risk or environmental requirement.
A planned movement pattern that reduces return from higher-risk areas into cleaner work.
A defined point where cleaning, clothing, tool or material controls change.

sections.title: Separate incompatible activities
sections.body: Waste handling, dirty-pot processing and symptomatic-plant work should not share immediate workflow with clean propagation or sanitized tools when avoidable.

sections.title: Movement is a contamination pathway
sections.body: Hands, carts, tools and clothing can move biological material among rooms. Map common routes before choosing sanitation controls.

sections.title: Safety belongs in layout decisions
sections.body: Access, egress, electrical equipment, wet work and material handling create worker hazards that should be considered before a room is densely loaded.

workedExamples: A harvest-waste cart crossing a clean propagation staging area creates a preventable workflow conflict.
A sanitation station placed after rather than before entry to a clean zone does not control incoming contamination.
commonMistakes: Using the same tools across zones without a defined decontamination step.
Blocking safe access with temporary crop expansion.
content.practicalApplication: Draw people, plant, supply, tool and waste movement on a room map. Mark crossings between clean and higher-risk activities and redesign the highest-risk intersections.
content.summary: Good layout reduces cross-contamination and worker risk by making intended movement obvious and repeatable.
